questions.problem:
Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[0,1]\times [0,1]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x. $$ Fill in the blanks in the matrix equation below that defines the first iteration of the Newton-Raphson process starting at the point $[1,\,1]^{T}.$
$[$ $2$ {{field-1}} $]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})\,=[$ $-3$ $]$
{{field-2}} $-4$ {{field-3}}
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}y-2{x}^{2}-2{y}^{2}+x)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-4x+1) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-4y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-4x+1) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-4y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6y-4 & 6x \\ 6x & -4\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-4x+1 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(1)-4 & 6(1) \\ 6(1) & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}6(1)(1)-4(1)+1 \\ 3(1)^{2}-4(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}2 & 6 \\ 6 & -4\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Suppose we wish to find a critical point of the function $f(x,y)$ in the region $[-2,2]\times [-3,3]⊆{R}^{2},$ where $$ f(x,y)=x{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}-8. $$ Calculate the second iteration of the Newton-Raphson process for optimization that starts at ${x}_{0}=[-2,\,-2]^{T}$ if the first iteration of the algorithm gives ${x}_{1}=[-1.4,\,0.4]^{T}.$ Round your final answer to three decimal places (if needed).
${x}_{2}≈[$ $-0.07$ $]$
{{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(x{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}-8) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(x{y}^{2}-2{x}^{2}+5{y}^{2}-8)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4x+{y}^{2} \\ 2xy+10y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(-4x+{y}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(2xy+10y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(-4x+{y}^{2}) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(2xy+10y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2y \\ 2y & 2x+10\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2y \\ 2y & 2x+10\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-4x+{y}^{2} \\ 2xy+10y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2y \\ 2y & 2x+10\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}-4x+{y}^{2} \\ 2xy+10y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2(0.4) \\ 2(0.4) & 2(-1.4)+10\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}-4(-1.4)+(0.4)^{2} \\ 2(-1.4)(0.4)+10(0.4)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0.8 \\ 0.8 & 7.2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}5.76 \\ 2.88\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{(-4)\cdot (7.2)-(0.8)\cdot (0.8)}[\begin{aligned}7.2 & -0.8 \\ -0.8 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5.76 \\ 2.88\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1.4 \\ 0.4\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{29.44}[\begin{aligned}39.168 \\ -16.128\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}-0.07 \\ -0.148\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

${x}_{2}≈[$ {{field-1}} $]$
$-0.221$
questions.worked_solution:
The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{3}-xy-{y}^{2}+3) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{3}-xy-{y}^{2}+3)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-y \\ -x-2y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-y) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(-x-2y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-y) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(-x-2y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6x & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson formula is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-{[\begin{aligned}6x & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-y \\ -x-2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

For the second iteration, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & ={x}_{1}-{[\begin{aligned}6x & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}3{x}^{2}-y \\ -x-2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{1}} \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.96 \\ -0.48\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}6(0.96) & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3(0.96)^{2}-(-0.48) \\ -0.96-2(-0.48)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.96 \\ -0.48\end{aligned}]-{[\begin{aligned}5.76 & -1 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}]}^{-1}[\begin{aligned}3.2448 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.96 \\ -0.48\end{aligned}]-\frac{1}{5.76\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot (-1)}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5.76\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3.2448 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.96 \\ -0.48\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{12.52}[\begin{aligned}-6.4896 \\ 3.2448\end{aligned}] \\  & ≈[\begin{aligned}0.442 \\ -0.221\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
